valuation_philosophy.summary: Accordant is a 100%-NZ staffing/recruitment holding company (AWF blue-collar labour hire, Madison/Absolute IT/JacksonStone/Hobson Leavy white-collar) coming off three consecutive loss-making years (FY24 -$10.0m incl. $11.0m goodwill impairment, FY25 -$2.9m, FY26 -$2.1m) and a dilutive May-2026 rescue rights issue (33.3m new shares at $0.15, 1.269 new shares per existing share) that raised $5.0m to pay down bank debt and secure covenant relief to April 2028. This is NOT a quality compounder DCF: there is no moat, margins are structurally thin (best pre-downturn owner-FCF margin was under 4%, and the FY19-23 ex-COVID average was ~2.15%), and the balance sheet carries ~$24m of pro-forma net bank debt against equity that is entirely goodwill/intangible-backed (tangible book value is NEGATIVE, roughly -$21.8m pro-forma once $31.6m goodwill and $13.1m other intangibles are stripped from the $22.9m pro-forma equity base).
valuation_philosophy.methodology: The DCF is built mid-cycle, not off trough (FY24-26) losses and not off the unrepeatable FY23 revenue peak ($227.4m) or FY21 COVID-distorted margin spike (8.72% owner-FCF margin, driven by wage-subsidy-era demand). Revenue is projected to recover gradually from the FY26 base ($165.1m) toward a mid-cycle range of $195-234m over a 10-year explicit horizon (10 years used because owner-FCF margins are still maturing well past year 5 -- Step 1c horizon-extension rule). EBITDA margin ramps toward ~4.5% (base case), anchored to the FY18/20/22/23 average (~4.2-4.8%), explicitly excluding the FY21 COVID spike (8.5%) and the weak FY19 print (2.9%). A high WACC (16-18%) is used to reflect four stacked, documented structural risk premiums on top of an 11-12% NZ small-cap base (see wacc_rationale). Terminal value uses the LOWER of Gordon-growth and an EV/EBITDA exit-multiple cap; in every scenario Gordon growth binds well below the cap, because owner-FCF conversion (mature ~2.0% of revenue) is structurally much thinner than the EBITDA margin (~4.5%) once realistic capex, IFRS-16 lease-principal cash outflows, 28% NZ statutory cash tax, and growth-linked working capital drag are deducted.
valuation_philosophy.conclusion: The DCF concludes that, on a pure cash-generation basis, Accordant's thin FCF conversion is insufficient to service its net debt load even after a full mid-cycle recovery is capitalized in perpetuity -- base and bear scenarios show NEGATIVE intrinsic equity value, and even the bull scenario (faster recovery + AI/automation margin uplift) is worth only $0.084/share, still below the current $0.166 price. This is consistent with -- not contradicted by -- the fact that the market currently prices AGL at roughly its historical-average EV/EBITDA multiple (~8.6x) on TROUGH FY26 EBITDA, and that tangible book value is already negative. AGL is best understood as a leveraged option on a NZ labour-market cyclical recovery and de-risking of the balance sheet, not as an undervalued cash-generative business. A margin-of-safety investor should treat the current price as pricing in recovery optimism the FCF economics do not yet support, and should look to the sanity-check multiples (not the FCF DCF alone) for a floor on downside.

premiums.detail: Market capitalisation ~NZ$11.2m post-raise (67.66m shares x $0.166); thin/irregular NZX trading volumes make exit difficult for any but the smallest positions

Group NPAT swung from +$6.2m (FY21) to -$10.0m (FY24), a ~$16m peak-to-trough swing on a business with historical shareholders' funds of only $20-40m; segment margins are low single digits with high operating leverage

Pro-forma net bank debt ~$24.0m vs market cap ~$11.2m and equity of $17.9m book value ($31.6m of which is goodwill); a rescue rights issue was needed in May-2026 to secure covenant relief; interest cover is tight (FY26 EBITDA $4.1m vs net finance costs $3.0m, ~1.4x cover)

Hull family trust holds 65.28% post-raise (up from 53.01%), having top-up funded the rescue raise; free float and independent institutional ownership are both very limited, and the board was streamlined (non-executive director departures) immediately post-raise

wacc_rationale.notes: Base case uses 17.0% (mid of the 16-18% range implied by summing the base + all four premiums at their midpoints). Bull case uses a lower 15.5% reflecting a scenario where the balance sheet de-risks faster and liquidity/governance premiums compress as the recovery is validated. Bear case uses 19.0% reflecting a renewed covenant scare (a real, named risk in the bear narrative) that would re-widen the leverage and illiquidity premiums.

inputs.net_debt_calc_note: Pro-forma net bank debt = $28.5m (31-Mar-2026 balance-date net bank debt) - $5.0m rights-offer gross proceeds + ~$0.5m raise costs = ~$24.0m. IFRS-16 lease liabilities ($12.7m at FY26) are EXCLUDED from net debt; lease principal repayments are instead deducted from owner FCF each year.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K/Annual Report Note F1: share-based payments expense $78,000 (FY2025: $123,000) -- confirmed genuinely immaterial (<0.1% of revenue every year), no adjustment needed beyond inclusion in owner-FCF build

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue and equity CAGRs are both deeply negative (three-year revenue -10.1%/yr, equity -19.7%/yr) reflecting the FY23-26 downturn and FY24 goodwill impairment. EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are not computable (negative/near-zero values in multiple years). Historical CAGRs are NOT used as the growth driver; projections are built bottom-up from a cyclical mid-cycle revenue recovery path anchored to FY19-23 pre-downturn levels (component build per Step 1c), not extrapolated from trailing CAGRs, because this is a post-trough cyclical recovery situation not a compounding growth trend.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF was negative or near-zero in FY24-26 (-0.91, -3.89, -0.78 $m) making FCF CAGR undefined. FY19-23 owner-FCF margins average 2.15% (ex-COVID FY20-21), the anchor for the mid-cycle margin used in projections. SBC is immaterial throughout (<$0.25m every year, <0.1% of revenue), so it is not a driver of the growth divergence here (unlike SBC-heavy growth names) -- the divergence is purely cyclical/impairment-driven.

base.ebitda_margin_anchor: Ramps from FY26 actual 2.48% toward 4.5% mature margin over 8 years, anchored to FY18/20/22/23 average (4.22%,4.63%,4.83%,4.13%; avg 4.45%), explicitly excluding FY21 COVID spike (8.47%) and weak FY19 (2.88%)
base.da_pct_note: Declines from FY26 actual 2.30% toward 1.80% mature level as lease-driven ROU depreciation normalizes
base.cash_tax_rate_note: NZ statutory rate applied flat; FY26 effective tax rate was 22.7% (FY25: 33.0%) with no valuation-allowance release or one-off credit identified, so no ramp is applied -- 28% is used as the conservative through-cycle assumption
base.terminal_cap_source: 10yr average post-IFRS16 (FY2021-FY2026, excl. FY2024 negative-EBITDA year) historical EV/EBITDA

bull.ebitda_margin_path: ramps FY26 2.48% -> 5.8% mature over 7yr (AI/automation productivity gains + operating leverage from faster volume recovery, approaching but not exceeding FY21 COVID-era 8.47% peak)

bear.ebitda_margin_path: ramps FY26 2.48% -> 3.2% mature over 8yr; recovery stalls, cost inflation offsets efficiency gains, another covenant scare assumed
bear.terminal_cap_source: 10yr historical minimum post-IFRS16 EV/EBITDA (FY2021, used as a floor consistent with renewed distress pricing)

probability_weighted.weighting_rationale: Bear weighted heavily (35%) given three consecutive loss-making years, a dilutive rescue rights issue completed just three months ago, negative tangible book value, and management having twice pushed back its own 'return to normal trading' guidance (first flagged for FY27 in the FY25 report, now FY27/FY28 again). Bull given only 20% given no evidence yet of the AI/automation margin thesis materialising and the government-procurement tailwind being modest and policy-dependent.

sanity_check.methodology_note: FY-end (31-Mar) closing prices and historical multiples computed on PRE-RAISE share counts (as reported at each balance date) since capital raise occurred post FY2026 year-end. FY2024 excluded from P/E average (net loss driven by $11.0m non-cash goodwill impairment).

trip_conditions_checked.result: not applicable -- base-case IV and current earnings both negative/near-zero, no meaningful P/E to test
implied P/B is -0.29x (negative equity value) -- far BELOW the historical range, not above
implied EV/EBITDA is 4.26x on FY26 trough EBITDA -- BELOW even the historical MINIMUM (3.61x), not above the max

trip_conditions_checked.condition: upside >100% while price in upper half of 10yr range
trip_conditions_checked.result: upside is -158% (base case); price ($0.166) is at the ABSOLUTE BOTTOM of the 10yr range ($0.145-$2.02), not the upper half

sanity_check.overall_result: PASS -- no trip conditions fired. All four conditions test for signs of an OVERVALUED model (assumptions too generous, implied multiples too rich, upside too large while price is already elevated). This DCF produces the opposite profile: implied multiples sit at or below the low end of AGL's own 10-year historical range, and the current price is already at the bottom of its 10-year range, consistent with the market pricing in real distress. No assumption tightening (deeper haircut, higher WACC, lower growth, lower exit caps) was required. If anything, the base-case assumptions (4.5% mature EBITDA margin, 28% cash tax, 12% WC capture, 0.35% capex) are already anchored conservatively to historical pre-downturn ex-COVID averages rather than to the FY23 revenue peak or FY21 COVID margin spike, and the negative base/bear equity values are corroborated independently by AGL's pro-forma tangible book value already being negative (~-$21.8m) purely from stripping goodwill/intangibles off reported equity -- i.e. two independent methods (cash-flow DCF and tangible-asset backing) both conclude the equity value is not well covered by hard assets or cash generation at the current debt load.

memo.rights_issue_dilution_warning: AGL completed a renounceable rights offer on 13-May-2026, issuing 33,333,334 new shares at $0.15/share (1.269 new shares per existing share) for $5.0m gross proceeds, taking shares on issue from 34,325,542 (the 31-Mar-2026 balance-date count) to 67,658,876. ALL historical per-share figures (price, EPS, DPS, book value per share) in filings and in the sanity_check block above are on the PRE-RAISE share count and are NOT directly comparable to post-raise per-share intrinsic values in this DCF. This DCF uses 67,658,876 shares (post-raise) throughout for all forward-looking per-share calculations (intrinsic value, entry price), consistent with the instruction to use the current, fully-diluted count.
memo.sbc_memo_value: Stock-based compensation is genuinely immaterial at AGL (FY2026: $78,000, or 0.047% of revenue; FY2025: $123,000). There is no meaningful spread between a 'SBC as non-cash' memo valuation and the reported owner-FCF valuation -- unlike SBC-heavy growth names, dilution/compensation treatment is not a material driver of this valuation. The dominant value drivers are instead: (1) the depth and duration of the cyclical margin recovery assumed, (2) the WACC applied given genuine balance-sheet and liquidity risk, and (3) whether Gordon-growth or the EV/EBITDA exit cap binds the terminal value.
memo.leverage_memo: Pro-forma net bank debt (~$24.0m) is intentionally NOT reduced further in this model beyond the actual May-2026 raise; no further capital raises, asset sales, or debt paydown beyond ordinary FCF generation are assumed in any scenario. Bank facilities are extended to April 2028 with covenants based on cumulative EBITDA, leverage ratio and interest cover -- a renewed covenant breach (explicitly the bear-case trigger) remains a live risk if the FY27/28 recovery stalls again, as management's own recovery timeline has already slipped once (FY27 guidance first given in the FY25 report).
